persona.role: founder of a two-year-old mobile app startup

sent_to_model:
yaar need help. Kavya from our accelerator batch put up a LinkedIn post yesterday about "founders in your own cohort DMing your team with 40% hikes" and everybody in the batch knows its about me, two of her engineers joined us earlier this month. 60+ comments already, people tagging me. I dont want to fight with her in public, she is genuinely a good friend and has helped me a lot. But some of what she said is just not true and I cant stay quiet also. I want to put up my own post, tag her, own the part where I messed up and clear the rest, and put the actual hike number in, 22 not 40, else people will keep repeating 40. Please dont name the two guys anywhere, they didnt ask for this. Keep it to 400-450 words and within 3,000 characters including spaces for LinkedIn. Please include my suggested cohort rule and coffee or call offer below.

- Foundry91 cohort 4, both of us, demo day was March 2026. her app SitterNest (babysitter booking), mine is DabbaDost (home tiffin subscriptions)
- we put a backend dev opening on our LinkedIn page and Instahyre on 14 Sept, open to anyone
- first guy applied himself on 19 Sept, second one came as his referral 2 weeks later. nobody from my side DMed anyone
- offer was 22% over their current CTC, not 40. both joined 3 Nov
- Kavya sat with me till 1am in the Koramangala office fixing our Razorpay webhook mess before demo day. never forgot that
- after the second offer got accepted I WhatsApped her, she left it on blue tick. then the post came
- she also said in post that we "promised ESOPs we dont even have". we have a pool, small, but its real and on paper since Jan
- my mistake - I knew where they worked from day one, I should have called her before making the offers, not after. thats on me
- in a batch of 11 startups this will keep happening, we hire from same small pool in HSR and Koramangala
- not a fight. want her to see I respect her
- suggest a simple rule for the cohort, if you are interviewing someone from another batch company you give that founder a heads up before the offer
- say coffee/call is open, this week, whenever she is ok

(About me: founder of a two-year-old mobile app startup, 35, Bengaluru, India. Length: it should come to 400-450 words, and no more than 3,000 characters.)

must_cover: Addresses and tags Kavya and acknowledges failing to call before making offers.
Corrects the recruitment and ESOP claims and states the actual 22 percent increase.
Proposes a cohort heads-up rule before offers.
Offers Kavya coffee or a call this week, whenever she is comfortable.
Communicates that the writer respects Kavya.
must_not_reveal: The names of the two engineers.
